text:
support: FYI customer acme-corp opened INT-4421 — p95->p99 tail jump on /v1/generate after last deploy. p95 ~90ms -> ~300ms, p99 ~1.2s. Affects tiny prompts (<50 tokens).

morgan: which route/model?

support: hosted / redwood/fast-v1, route=small-prompt-pool, region=us-east-1.

ava: checking metrics — looks like cohorting behavior. cohort_wait_ms spiked and cohorts are filling to 16 items before dispatch. tiny requests are being held to fill batches -> increases tail.

sam: can you paste the batching config for that route?

support: sure, current config from console:

```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  cohort_wait_ms: 80
  cohort_max_items: 16
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  flush_threshold: 0.75
  small_prompt_policy: route_to_shared
```

ava: logs show repeated lines like: "waiting for cohort completion" then "batch dispatched size=16"; trace ids show individual request wait time ~700-1100ms depending on arrival. p99 aligns with batch fill latency.

morgan: repro steps? want to run locally vs canary.

support: repro: run 1k single-token prompts concurrently against route small-prompt-pool. curl example: `curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` in a tight loop. Attaching trace id 2027a8 for one example.

sam: short-term mitigation options: reduce cohort_wait_ms to 10ms for that route, or set cohort_max_items=4, or enable instant_flush_on_small_prompts: true. All will reduce tail but may raise token cost.

ava: agree. Another quick mitigation is min_batch_size=1 override for that route so tiny requests are flushed immediately. Tradeoff: less batching efficiency.

morgan: I'll push a canary config change: cohort_wait_ms=10 for small-prompt-pool on 2 nodes and monitor p95/p99.

infra-bot: deploy started: config-update cohort_wait_ms=10 for route=small-prompt-pool (canary nodes 2/10).

morgan: canary metrics after 5m: p95 ~85ms, p99 ~160ms for the repro workload. Good signal. Rolling to remaining nodes.

support: Customer notified about interim fix and ETA for full rollout. They asked to keep an option to revert if cost impact is too high.

sam: longer-term: we should implement auto-tune for cohort_wait based on observed request size distribution and add a policy to auto-route very small requests to a low-latency pool (single-request capacity). Also consider prefix caching for repeated tiny prompts.

ava: created OPS-552: "Analyze request length distribution and implement cohort auto-tune + low-latency pool". Assigned to morgan.

morgan: acknowledged, will add a dashboard tile showing small_prompt_fraction and a playbook with rollback steps.

ava: follow-up action: add alert rule: WHEN p99_route > 500ms AND small_prompt_fraction > 40% for 5m -> page oncall + post slack #eng-sre.

sam: added to alerting backlog, will draft rule.

support: closing loop with customer for now, will keep them updated on OPS-552.

morgan: pro tip — when tuning, watch burstiness: lowering cohort_wait too far can hurt throughput. aim for adaptive e.g., start 80ms, if small_prompt_fraction>50% reduce to 10ms for 10min, then reassess.

ava: thanks all. marking thread resolved once OPS-552 is triaged. :white_check_mark:
